title: Versioned run identity for the curator cache
description: Add versioned run identity to the curator cache, replacing the ad-hoc fingerprint. Create a new top-level module `src/bespokelabs/curator/run_identity.py` (top-level, not under `llm/`, so `db.py` can import from it without a cycle) exporting `RUN_IDENTITY_VERSION: int = 3` and `RUN_IDENTITY_FILENAME: str = "run_identity.json"`; the exception family `RunIdentityError(RuntimeError)`, `RunIdentityMismatch(RunIdentityError)`, `CachedResponseMismatch(RunIdentityError)`; the frozen dataclasses `RunIdentity(run_hash, digest, identity_version, cache_enabled, components)`, `RunStamp(identity_version, run_hash, digest, components, created_at, updated_at)` with `to_dict()` / `from_dict()`, and `RunDirectoryCheck(status, stamp, previous_version)`; and the functions `compute_run_identity(llm, dataset_hash, *, cache_enabled: bool = True, run_id: Optional[str] = None) -> RunIdentity`, `write_run_stamp(run_cache_dir, identity, *, now: str, created_at: Optional[str] = None) -> RunStamp`, `read_run_stamp(run_cache_dir) -> Optional[RunStamp]` (returns `None` when the file is absent or unreadable; it does not raise), and `reconcile_run_directory(run_cache_dir, identity, *, now: str) -> RunDirectoryCheck`, which decides what a run does with the directory it is about to use and stamps it. The identity duck-types its `llm` argument (no `isinstance`, no import of `LLM`) and reads `llm.prompt_formatter.{prompt_func, parse_func, model_name, response_format, generation_params, system_prompt}`, `llm.batch_mode`, `llm.backend`, `llm.backend_params` and `llm.return_completions_object`, plus the dataset hash and the optional run id; the two function components use `_get_function_hash`, which moves verbatim out of `llm/llm.py` into this module and stays importable from its old home; `digest` is an `xxh64` hexdigest over a deterministic JSON serialisation of the components, and `run_hash` is the name of the run's cache directory. The module reads no clock and no randomness — every timestamp and every run id arrives as a parameter — and `write_run_stamp` writes the six-key stamp (`identity_version`, `run_hash`, `digest`, `components`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) into `RUN_IDENTITY_FILENAME` in the run directory, `created_at` defaulting to `now`, `updated_at` always `now`. Wire it up: `llm.py` deletes `_hash_fingerprint()` in favour of `LLM._run_identity(dataset_hash, *, cache_enabled, run_id=None)`, adds `backend` and `backend_params` properties (`backend_params` is a copy of what was passed to `__init__`, `{}` when `None`), takes a `run_id` keyword on `__call__` (defaulting from `CURATOR_RUN_ID` or a fresh `uuid4().hex`) and reconciles the run directory before using it, and `_get_cached_response` re-raises `RunIdentityError` while still returning `None` with the existing warning for every other exception; `db.py` gains `RUNS_COLUMNS`, writes `parse_func` and `identity_version`, and `validate_schema()` migrates missing columns forward and returns the tuple it added while still rejecting unexpected ones; `types/curator_response.py` gains `run_identity: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None` declared last and emitted by `to_dict()`, and `load(cache_dir, dataset, *, verify: bool = True)` checks the recorded dataset block against the dataset it is handed and raises `CachedResponseMismatch`; and `BaseRequestProcessor.run()` resets `_is_cached_dataset` as its first statement. No new dependency; Python 3.10 target.

requirement.rule: Of everything in `llm.backend_params`, exactly four keys participate in the run key — `azure_deployment`, `base_url`, `batch_size`, `completion_window`, declared as the module constant `IDENTITY_BACKEND_PARAM_KEYS: frozenset[str]` — and every other backend param is dropped before the components are serialised or hashed; the `backend` component is the backend name the request processor resolved (`self._request_processor.backend`), not the `backend=` argument the caller declared.
requirement.scope: Applies to the identity component dict for any duck-typed llm object, and therefore to `run_hash`, to the cache directory name, and to the `components` block written into `run_identity.json`. Only the identity's view is filtered: the full `backend_params` dict still reaches the request processor unchanged, and `LLM.backend_params` still returns all of it.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: Changing `api_key`, `max_retries`, `request_timeout`, `require_all_responses`, `batch_check_interval`, `max_requests_per_minute`, `seconds_to_pause_on_rate_limit` or `delete_successful_batch_files` must leave `run_hash` byte-identical, so the run lands in the same directory and still hits cache — `api_key` is excluded deliberately even though it changes what comes back, because the components are written to disk in cleartext. Changing `base_url`, `batch_size`, `completion_window` or `azure_deployment` must fork the run. `LLM(model_name="gpt-4o-mini")` and `LLM(model_name="gpt-4o-mini", backend="openai")` are the same run.
requirement.failure_behavior: A component value that `json.dumps` cannot serialise raises `RunIdentityError` — no `default=str`, no `repr` fallback, and no bare `TypeError` escaping.
requirement.observability: With stub `S` whose `backend_params == {"base_url": "https://x/v1", "max_retries": 7, "api_key": "sk-secret", "request_timeout": 30}`: `compute_run_identity(S, "d0").components["backend_params"] == {"base_url": "https://x/v1"}`; `compute_run_identity(S, "d0").run_hash == compute_run_identity(S2, "d0").run_hash` where `S2` differs only in `max_retries=999, api_key="sk-other"`; a differing `base_url` gives a different `run_hash`; and after the stamp is written, `"sk-secret"` appears nowhere in `run_identity.json` on disk.

fragmentation_sources: engineering-chat thread arguing which backend knobs should fork the cache, ending in the four-key list
wiki page documenting what the run directory contains and that it is world-readable cleartext
code-review email objecting that api_key was being hashed into a file on disk
support thread where a user retuned max_retries and lost a finished batch cache
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An earlier build hashed the whole `backend_params` dict (api_key and retry knobs included) the same way `generation_params` is hashed today; reversed once the components started being written to disk in cleartext and retry-tuning began forking caches.

requirement.rule: `reconcile_run_directory` reports one of exactly four status strings on `RunDirectoryCheck.status`: `"created"` when the directory is missing or exists with zero entries (create it with `parents=True, exist_ok=True`, write the stamp, `previous_version=None`); `"adopted"` when it is non-empty but carries no readable stamp (write the stamp, delete nothing, `previous_version=None`); `"upgraded"` when the stamp's `identity_version` is below `RUN_IDENTITY_VERSION` (rewrite it under the current identity while preserving the old stamp's `created_at`, `previous_version` = the old int); `"matched"` when the stamp is the current version with the same `run_hash` and equal `components` (refresh `updated_at` only, `previous_version=3`).
requirement.scope: Runs against the run cache directory named by `run_hash`, before the run reads or writes anything else in it, on every `LLM.__call__` — including disabled-cache directories, which are reconciled the same way.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: A non-empty, stamp-less directory from a pre-v3 cache is adopted and left intact — not refused and not cleared, the opposite of this repo's habit of raising and telling the user to `rm -rf ~/.cache/curator`; the corrupt-arrow-file path in `attempt_loading_cached_dataset` keeps its own clear-and-rerun behaviour and is not folded into reconciliation.
requirement.failure_behavior: Disagreement raises `RunIdentityMismatch` and leaves the directory byte-for-byte untouched (no stamp rewrite, no file created or deleted). The exception carries `path`, `expected_run_hash`, `found_run_hash` and `mismatched_components`: a stamp whose `identity_version` is above `RUN_IDENTITY_VERSION` gives `mismatched_components == ("identity_version",)`; a current-version stamp with a different `run_hash` or differing components gives the alphabetically sorted tuple of the component keys whose values differ, or `("run_hash",)` when the stamp carries no comparable components.
requirement.observability: Empty `tmp_path/"a"` → `status == "created"`, `previous_version is None`, `len(os.listdir(a)) == 1`. `tmp_path/"b"` holding `payload.txt` → `status == "adopted"`, `previous_version is None`, `sorted(os.listdir(b)) == ["payload.txt", "run_identity.json"]` with `payload.txt` unchanged. `tmp_path/"c"` pre-stamped `identity_version=2, created_at="2024-06-01T00:00:00"` → `status == "upgraded"`, `previous_version == 2`, stamp now version 3 with `created_at` still `"2024-06-01T00:00:00"`; reconciled again → `status == "matched"`, `previous_version == 3`, only `updated_at` moves. `tmp_path/"d"` stamped `identity_version=4` → `RunIdentityMismatch` with `mismatched_components == ("identity_version",)`. `tmp_path/"e"` stamped with another identity differing in `model_name` and `parse_func_hash` → `RunIdentityMismatch` with `mismatched_components == ("model_name", "parse_func_hash")`, `found_run_hash` equal to the stamp's hash, and `os.listdir(e)` unchanged.

fragmentation_sources: incident thread where a stale-cache raise told a user to delete their cache and they lost a finished batch run
design-doc comment settling the four status words and what each one is allowed to touch on disk
chat exchange about pre-existing cache directories from before the stamp landed, and whether to trust them
review email asking the mismatch error to say which components differed, in a stable order, for the bug template
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The first cut followed `validate_schema`'s house style: any unrecognised or unstamped directory raised `RuntimeError` pointing at `rm -rf ~/.cache/curator`, and stamp-less directories were briefly wiped and re-created; reversed to adopt-and-stamp, upgrade-in-place, and raise-without-touching-files.

brief:
Run cache identity: what makes two curator runs "the same run", and what a caller
gets back when the cache says they are.

The area, concretely:
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/llm/llm.py` — `_hash_fingerprint()` (line 144), which
  joins five things with `_` (lines 151-159: `dataset_hash`, `prompt_func_hash`,
  `model_name`, the `response_format` JSON schema, `batch_mode`) plus
  `generation_params` when set (lines 161-163) and xxh64s the result; the
  `disable_cache` branch (lines 145-146), which hashes `os.urandom(8)` instead, so
  every such run mints a fresh directory nothing ever removes; `__call__`
  (line 187), where `run_cache_dir = os.path.join(curator_cache_dir, fingerprint)`
  (line 224) is created before anything about it is validated; and
  `_get_function_hash()` (line 337), which pickles the function with
  `datasets.utils._dill` after mutating `func.__annotations__ = {}`.
- The things the fingerprint does NOT contain, each of which changes what comes
  back: `parse_func` — hashed separately at line 274 and handed to the processor
  as `parse_func_hash`; the backend and `backend_params`; and
  `return_completions_object`.
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/request_processor/base_request_processor.py` —
  `attempt_loading_cached_dataset()` (line 363), the second cache key: a file
  named `f"{parse_func_hash}.arrow"` (line 372) INSIDE the directory the first key
  chose, deleted and regenerated on `pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid` (lines 378-384).
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/db.py` — `MetadataDB`, the third account of the same
  run. `validate_schema()` (line 30) lists fourteen `expected_columns` (line 38)
  and raises `RuntimeError` telling the user to `rm -rf ~/.cache/curator` on any
  mismatch; `store_metadata()` (line 64) is handed a dict that also carries
  `timestamp` and `parse_func` (`llm.py` lines 253-262), and its INSERT (line 126)
  writes ten columns — dropping `parse_func` silently, and never writing any of
  the four `total_*` cost columns the schema declares (lines 49-52).
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/types/curator_response.py` — `save()` (line 297) and
  `load()` (line 314), the fourth. `to_dict()` (line 248) records the dataset's
  `fingerprint`, size and columns; `load(cache_dir, dataset)` takes the dataset it
  is handed and never compares it against what was recorded.
  `_get_cached_response()` (`llm.py` line 171) swallows every exception from it and
  returns `None`.

Four layers disagree about what makes two runs the same run, and the disagreement
is reachable. Change only the parse function and the fingerprint is identical, so
the run lands in the same directory, the same `response.json` is overwritten, and
the caller gets back whichever parse function ran last. Change the backend or
`backend_params` and none of the four keys notices. Set `CURATOR_DISABLE_CACHE`
and a directory and a metadata row are minted per run under a random `run_hash`,
and neither is ever collected. Read all four and design the fix as one fully
specified run-identity rule: what participates in the key, where the key is
written down so a later run can check it, and what happens when what is on disk
was written under a different one.

Constraints: pure and deterministic, no network, no sleeping, no threads. The
clock and any source of randomness are injected, never read from `datetime`,
`time` or `os.urandom` inside the identity code. The design must be testable by
calling the key function directly on an LLM-shaped object, by driving `MetadataDB`
against a temp-file database, and by round-tripping `CuratorResponse.save`/`load`
on a small in-memory `datasets.Dataset` — no provider, no event loop, no viewer
client.
